texto: Measure Takeoff is plan takeoff for trade contractors: open the PDF plans in the browser, set the scale, measure walls, floors, siding, windows and doors with the mouse, and KORbuild turns the measurements into materials and labor hours through assemblies. From there it builds the material list for supplier quotes and the proposal for the client. Measure Takeoff is for the people who estimate: they open the plans, measure and issue the proposal that goes to the client.

Feet and inches, the way estimators work. Every length is shown as 12'-6 1/2" and every area in sq ft; you can type dimensions the same way. Behind the scenes, KORbuild keeps exact numbers, so zoom and screen size never change a measurement. Measure Takeoff once, get everything. A wall measured once produces studs, plates, sheathing, house wrap, insulation, drywall and the carpenter hours. Count one more window and the sheathing, drywall and siding already account for it. Every number can be explained. Each material shows the math behind it: which condition, which formula, the waste % and the

Owner / admin Computer Also maintains the catalog: items, assemblies with formulas, prices and markups. Measuring needs a mouse and a large screen: Measure Takeoff is used on a computer.

Screen What it shows Projects Every estimate with client, location, type, estimator, bid due date (with alerts) and status: Estimating, Proposal sent, Won, Lost. Project The project data, the sheets (with scale status), the quantities per condition, the typicals and the materials and labor. Links to the material list and the proposal. Sheet (viewer) The plan full screen, the conditions on the left, the toolbar (Pan, Measure Takeoff, Deduct, Opening, Typical, scale, zoom). Items The catalog of what you buy or pay for, in purchase units, with cost code. Assemblies Groups of items with formulas,

Step What happens 1. Project Create it with client, location and bid due date. 2. Plans Upload the PDF: each page becomes a sheet. 3. Scale Pick the scale from the list (or calibrate from a dimension) and check it on another dimension. 4. Add assemblies Choose what you will measure on this sheet (exterior walls, flooring, siding, windows…). 5. Measure Takeoff Click on the plan: lines, areas, counts. Deduct openings and cut-outs. 6. Materials and labor Calculated from the assemblies, with the math visible. 7. Quotes Send each supplier its list; enter the prices they send back. 8. Proposal Price

Step by step, from the PDF plan to the proposal. The screenshots come from a demo account with sample data, signed in as Tom Reilly (Admin at Northfield Framing & Siding), with the sample project Model home. Use a computer Measuring needs a mouse and a large screen. Measure Takeoff is designed for a computer; on a phone, it will be read-only (see Release status).

What it is for: keeping every estimate in one list, with the bid due dates in sight. Who can do it Anyone with Measure Takeoff plans (default roles: Admin and Project manager). Open Measure Takeoff: the Projects list shows each project with its client, location, type, estimator, bid due date and status. The tabs filter by status: Estimating, Proposal sent, Won, Lost. While a project is Estimating, the bid due date is highlighted when it is overdue, today or within 3 days. The project list

Click New project. Fill in the project and the client (choose from your contacts, or create one without leaving the form), the job location (address, city, state, ZIP) and the proposal data (bid due date, estimator, and the job it belongs to, for change orders or additions). Click Create project. The project form Name, client, city and state are required. To change the project later, open it and click Edit project; Delete is in the edit form.

Open the project. Click Upload PDF and choose the plan set. Each page becomes a sheet (A-101, A-201…). The Sheets table shows each sheet's scale: no scale, checked or scale check off. A project with its sheets

Why: every measurement depends on the scale. Checking it on a second dimension catches plans printed or scanned off scale. Open a sheet (Open). The plan fills the screen, with the conditions on the left. Click the scale button on the toolbar (Set scale, in amber, while the sheet has none). Pick the scale written on the plan (for example, 1/4" = 1'-0") and click Use this scale. If the plan is off scale, use Calibrate from a dimension: click both ends of a known dimension and type its length. Choosing the sheet scale KORbuild asks you to check: click both ends of another known dimension and type

The drawing starts empty. You add one assembly for each thing you will measure on this sheet: the assembly brings the materials and labor that the measurement will produce. In the conditions panel, click Add assembly. Choose an assembly. The list is grouped by type — Linear (walls), Area (floors, siding, slabs) and Count (doors, windows) — with a summary of its lines. Assemblies already on the drawing are marked. Just measure, no assembly creates a condition without materials (you can apply an assembly later). Select a condition in the panel; the Measure Takeoff tool is on. Type How to measure Count One click per item. Linear Click each point. Double-click or Enter finishes, Esc cancels, Backspace removes the last point. Area Same as linear; a click on the first point also closes the area. Shift keeps the line straight (horizontal or vertical). Near (6 px) an existing point, the click snaps to it; Alt turns snapping off. Hold the space bar (or use Pan) to drag the plan. Ctrl + mouse wheel zooms at the cursor; Fit shows the whole sheet. Zoom never changes a measurement. While drawing, the dashed line

On an area (a floor, for example), choose Deduct and draw the polygon to take out (stairs, a chimney, a bathroom with another finish). It appears hatched in red, with "− X sq ft", and is listed as a cut-out.

Windows and doors are counts with an opening size (width × height). Walls and siding that deduct them lose that area automatically: count one more window and the sheathing, drywall and siding already change. On an elevation, the Opening tool goes further: Choose Opening and click two opposite corners of the window or door. Choose which count it is (it adds +1) and confirm the areas behind it to deduct from. Click Count and deduct. Opening drawn on the east elevation Siding measured on the elevations, with windows, door and a drawn opening An opening already cut out by drawing is not deducted a

What it is for: measuring once what repeats — the typical floor, the typical apartment, the same house built six times. The whole sheet repeats: in the panel, click This sheet repeats (typical floor, repeated house) and enter the occurrences (for example, Building A × 3 and Building B × 3). Only part of the sheet repeats: choose Typical on the toolbar, click two corners of the region and enter the occurrences. Everything measured inside counts × the total of occurrences — quantities, materials, quote lists and the proposal. The project shows, for each typical, the quantity per unit, per occurr

Back on the project (the project name, at the left of the viewer's toolbar): Quantities: each condition with its measured total, its derived values (for example, Surface (× height)) and the number of measurements. Quantities per condition Materials and labor: every item in its purchase unit (sheets, boxes, rolls, pieces, hours), grouped by category, with the estimated labor hours. Click an item to see the math: condition → variables → formula → waste → rounding. On the project, click Material list for quotes. Check Reply by, Deliver to and the Notes for the supplier. Each supplier gets its own list — only the items in the cost codes it supplies (Settings › Contacts) — in purchase units, already with waste and rounding, without prices and without labor. For each supplier: Send by email opens the email ready, with the list and the reply-by date; PDF opens the quote request with your logo and blank price columns; Enter prices received records the prices the supplier sent back: they become the items' prices from that date. What it is for: knowing the cost of every item and how it becomes a selling price. Open Pricing: Markups: overhead % and profit, as markup (on cost) or margin (share of the selling price), and sales tax on materials. New version creates new markups from a date, with a reason; the old ones stay in the history. Items: the current price of each item, since when and where it came from (sample price list, typed in, a supplier quote). New price adds a price from a date; nothing is overwritten. On the project, click Proposal. Review the Scope (it comes from the project). Proposal items: one line per cost code, materials and labor together. Each line shows the basis (quantities and estimated hours), the cost, and the calculated price (catalog prices + markups). Type a different amount whenever you want (a closed price); clear it to go back to the calculated price. Uncheck a line to leave it out; add other items (mobilization, dumpster…). Show material quantities on the document is optional. Check the validity and the terms (they come from the company profile and can be adjusted). View

Who can do it Anyone with Items and assemblies (default role: Admin). Without it, items and formulas are read-only. Items (Measure Takeoff › Items) are what you buy or pay for: code, name, purchase unit, category (material, labor, equipment, subcontractor), cost code and notes. An item used in an assembly cannot be deleted. The item catalog Assemblies (Measure Takeoff › Assemblies) are lists of lines for a type of condition. Each line has: Column What it is Item What the line produces, in its purchase unit. Formula The raw quantity, using the condition's variables (for example, NetSurfaceArea

What it is for: when a general contractor (or another company) invites yours to bid through KORbuild, the invitation arrives in Measure Takeoff and you answer it there. Open Invitations in the Measure Takeoff menu. The bell also warns you when a new invitation arrives. Open the invitation: the package (cost codes, drawings, due date, requirements) and the history. Use Questions and messages to ask the contractor before the due date. Click I'll bid or Decline (with an optional reason the contractor sees). I'll bid creates a project in Measure Takeoff with the drawings already attached. Measure,

Message What it means What to do no scale (sheet) The sheet has no scale yet; measuring is disabled. Set and check the scale. off (scale) The check dimension differs by more than 1%. Calibrate from a dimension, or zoom in and check again. Missing on the condition: … An assembly line needs a property the condition does not have (height, thickness, pitch). Edit the condition and add it. nothing measured yet An assembly is on the drawing but has no measurements. Measure Takeoff it, or delete it. Formula refused The formula uses something not allowed, divides by zero or gives a negative result. Fi

Each rule has an ID (MSR-nnn) so it can be quoted in meetings, tests and change requests. The Status column says whether the rule works today. Source These rules come from the product and from the Measure Takeoff specification. Open points are marked To be confirmed at the end.

ID Rule Status MSR-001 No fractions or text in the math. Lengths are stored in inches, areas in square inches, volumes in cubic inches. Feet and inches appear only on screen. Working MSR-002 Points are stored in the PDF page's coordinates, never in screen pixels. Zoom and screen resolution never change a measurement. Working MSR-003 The scale belongs to the sheet. It comes from the list (architectural and engineering scales) or from calibrating on a known dimension. Each sheet has its own scale. Working MSR-004 Scale check: after setting the scale, measure another known dimension. A difference

ID Rule Status MSR-010 A condition is what you measure (exterior walls, LVP floor, siding, windows W1). It has a name, a type, a color and properties, and measurements on one or more sheets. Working MSR-011 Three types: linear (with height → surface; with pitch → pitched length), area (with pitch → roof area; with thickness → volume) and count. Working MSR-012 Openings: a count (window, door) can have a width and a height. A wall or an area can deduct the openings of chosen counts, from any sheet of the project. Counting one more window updates the sheathing, the drywall and the siding. Workin

ID Rule Status MSR-020 An item is what you buy or pay for, in its purchase unit (sheet, box, roll, piece, cu yd, hour), with a category (material, labor, equipment, subcontractor) and a cost code (CSI MasterFormat). Working MSR-021 An assembly is a set of lines for one type of condition. One measurement feeds many items. Working MSR-022 A formula only calculates the raw quantity. Waste % and rounding (none, or up to 1, 0.5 or 0.25) are separate columns, never numbers hidden in the formula. Working MSR-023 Variables in trade units, with the names US estimators use: MeasuredLinear, MeasuredArea,

ID Rule Status MSR-030 Name, client, city and state are required; state with 2 letters, ZIP with 5 digits (or 5+4). Working MSR-031 Status: Estimating → Proposal sent → Won or Lost. The bid due date alerts (overdue, today, within 3 days) only while Estimating. Working MSR-032 Deleting a project deletes its sheets and conditions, after confirmation. Working

ID Rule Status MSR-040 A typical has a name, a region of the sheet (or the whole sheet) and its occurrences: where it repeats and how many times, counting the one drawn (e.g., Building A 3 + Building B 3 = × 6). Working MSR-041 A measurement belongs to the typical when its center falls inside the region; it counts × the total of occurrences. Working MSR-042 The multiplication applies everywhere: condition totals, openings, formula variables, materials, quote lists and the proposal. Working MSR-043 Typicals do not overlap, and a whole-sheet typical cannot coexist with regions on the same sheet

ID Rule Status MSR-050 The material list for quotes has only materials (no labor), in purchase units, with waste and rounding, split by supplier: each supplier gets only the cost codes it supplies (Settings › Contacts). Items nobody supplies go to "No supplier". Working MSR-051 Suppliers never see selling prices, labor or formulas. Working MSR-052 Prices a supplier sends back can be entered on the list; they become the item's price from that date, with the source "Quote · supplier". What each person can do in Measure Takeoff comes from their access role (Settings › Access roles). The company can adjust the default roles or create new ones.

Permission What it allows Measure Takeoff plans Open Measure Takeoff: projects, upload PDFs, set the scale, measure, add and apply assemblies, see quantities and materials, material lists for quotes and proposals. Items and assemblies Create and edit items, assemblies with formulas, prices and markups. Includes Measure Takeoff plans. Without it, formulas and prices are read-only.

Role Measure Takeoff Items and assemblies Notes Admin ✓ ✓ Usually the owner or the chief estimator. Project manager ✓ — Measures and prices, but does not change the catalog. Foreman — — Does not see Measure Takeoff. Worker — — Does not see Measure Takeoff. Good to know Measure Takeoff is offered to companies that do the work (subcontractors, or companies that both hire and do the work). A general contractor does not have Measure Takeoff: it receives the proposal by email or PDF. Measure Takeoff is the first KORbuild release. It runs on the cloud database, in the browser of a computer. This page says what works today and what comes next.

Item How it works Projects, plans and takeoff Projects, PDF plans (kept in your company's cloud storage), scale, conditions with their measurements and typicals are saved as you work. Open the same takeoff on another computer and it is all there. Two people on the same condition: the second is warned and sees the saved version. Catalog, prices and markups Your company's own items and assemblies. Prices and markups are versions with an effective date; they never change or disappear, and the author is recorded. Dollar amounts are visible only to people with the catalog permission or cost visibil

Item Notes Computer only Measuring needs a mouse and a large screen. Use a computer with Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Email Quote requests and proposals open in your email program with the message ready; you attach the PDF (Save as PDF). Click precision Each click lands on a whole screen pixel; at normal zoom that is about 3/4" per point. The scale check shows the error, and a larger zoom reduces it.

Item Notes Sending by KORbuild Quote requests and proposals sent by KORbuild, with the PDF attached and a record of what was sent. Snapping Clicks snapping to the lines of vector PDFs. Measure on the phone Read-only: projects, quantities, materials, quote lists and issued proposals. Drawing stays on the computer. More assemblies and trades Roofing, drywall, concrete and others, with formulas from each trade.

Bids is how one company invites others to bid on a scope of work, compares the bids and awards one — all inside KORbuild. The company that hires is the contracting company: a general contractor hiring subcontractors, or a subcontractor passing part of its work to another one (subcontracting). The invited companies bid from Measure Takeoff when they have a KORbuild account, or through a private link when they do not. An invitation can go from any company to any company: general contractor to subcontractor, general contractor to general contractor, or subcontractor to subcontractor. Bids come wi

One place for the whole bid. Package, invitations, answers, questions, bids, leveling and award — no spreadsheets and email threads to reconcile. Each company sees only its own. An invited company never sees who else was invited, the others' amounts or the winning amount. Leveling that tells the truth. A cost code without a price shows as not bid, never as zero; an exclusion that is in your included scope is flagged before you award. The award links the two jobs. The winner creates its job from the won project and it is already linked to the contracting company's job.

Who Where What they do Contracting company (admin, project manager) Bids Builds the package, invites, answers questions, levels the bids, awards. Invited company with KORbuild (admin, estimator) Measure Takeoff › Invitations Opens the invitation, bids or declines, measures in a project created from it and submits through the platform. Invited company without KORbuild A private link Sees the invitation, answers, asks and submits the bid PDF with the total. No account needed.

Step What happens 1. Package The contracting company describes the scope, picks the cost codes and the due date, and chooses the invitees from its Contacts. 2. Invitations Each invitee gets it in KORbuild (with an account) or by a private link (without one). 3. Answer I'll bid creates a project in Measure Takeoff; Decline can carry a reason. 4. Questions Each answer goes to all invitees (without saying who asked) or only to who asked. 5. Bids Submitted through the platform, by cost code. Each new one is a revision; nothing is edited. 6. Step by step. The screenshots come from a demo account with sample data: Ana Ribeiro (Admin at Example Builders, the general contractor) sends and awards, Tom Reilly (Admin at Northfield Framing & Siding) bids, and Bay State Drywall answers by link, without an account.

What it is for: inviting companies to bid on a scope of work. Who can do it Anyone with Run bids and award (default roles: Admin and Project manager). Open Bids in the Measure Takeoff menu (or Get sub bids on a project). The list has tabs Open, Ready to award, Drafts, Awarded and All. Bids Click New bid. Fill in the package: Scope of work: the project and a name (e.g. Framing and drywall). Cost codes to bid: check the ones that apply (they come from your catalog and suppliers) or type others. Each one becomes a row in the leveling. Included and Excluded scope, one item per line; notes (work ho

The bid page opens on Invitees: each company, how it receives (KORbuild or link), its status (Invitation sent, Viewed, Will bid, Declined with the reason, Bid submitted), its latest bid and when it viewed the invitation. Invitees Extend: a new due date, after the current one; invitees can bid until then. Invite more: companies not invited yet. Cancel: with a reason; invitees are notified. Copy the link: for an invitee without an account.

The Questions tab has one conversation per invitee, and the count of questions without an answer. Click Reply under a question. Write the answer and choose All invitees (the question goes along, without saying who asked) or Only the one who asked. Use Notify all for an addendum, a date change or a new sheet. Questions

Level bids shows one column per bid and one row per cost code, next to your budget: in green, the lowest amount of each cost code; not bid when a company left a cost code without a price — compare totals only between complete bids; duration, exclusions (⚠ when an exclusion is in your included scope), date and proposal number. Leveling Click Award on the chosen column. The confirmation warns about cost codes not bid and exclusions in scope. After Award, the bid is closed and never changes; the others are told they were not selected, without the amount. If the bid came from a project of yours th

What it is for: answering an invitation and submitting your bid without leaving KORbuild. Who can do it Anyone with Respond to invitations and submit bids (default roles: Admin and Project manager). Open Measure Takeoff › Invitations (the bell also tells you). Open the invitation: the package, the due date, the budget if the contracting company chose to show it. Click I'll bid — KORbuild creates a project in Measure Takeoff with the contracting company, the address and the due date — or Decline, with an optional reason the contracting company sees. A company can hire another one for part of its work, with the same screens. On your Measure Takeoff project, Get sub bids › New bid. The due date must be before your own. In Level bids, Use in my estimate puts the sub's price into your project proposal (as other items, with your markups). You award only after you win and create the job. If the company that hired you asked for approval, Award sends it a request: it sees only the company you chose, never the amount, and approves or declines. If it does not allow subcontracting, the bid is not sent. A subcontracting bid

Permission What it allows Run bids and award Create and send bids, extend, invite more, answer questions, level, award and cancel; sees the bid amounts. Respond to invitations and submit bids See invitations, I'll bid or Decline, ask questions and submit bids through the platform. Includes Measure plans.

Role Run bids Respond to invitations Admin ✓ ✓ Project manager ✓ ✓ Foreman and Worker — — Good to know Dollar amounts stay with the parties. The leveling is only for who has Run bids and award. Settings is where your company sets up KORbuild once: the company profile, the contacts, the people who use the system and what each of them can do. Each company has its own Settings and never sees another company's.

Screen What it is for Company Name, legal name, address, phone, logo and the details that appear on proposals. Jobs One entry per job. Needed to close a bid: the company that wins creates its job from the won project, already linked to the contracting company's job. Contacts Clients, suppliers and other companies you work with. A supplier is marked with the cost codes it supplies, so each quote list goes to the right supplier. Contacts are not users: they receive the quote request or the proposal by email and need no account. Users The people who sign in. Invite by email, choose each person's

Entered once. A contact created in Settings is used in every project, quote list and proposal. Every change has an author. Changes to users, roles and the company are recorded with who did them and when. Language. Each person chooses English or Portuguese; the guide and the screens follow.
Step by step, one task at a time. Settings is under the Settings tab of your account (the page you land on after signing in).
Open Company. Fill in the name, legal name, address, phone and email. These details appear on your proposals. Add the logo (optional) and save.

Open Jobs and choose New job, or open a won project in Measure Takeoff and click Create job from this project (name, address and parties come filled in). Fill in the client, the location (click the map or use your current location) and the start and end dates. Project and job stay linked. When the project won a bid, the job is created already linked to the contracting company's job.

Open Contacts and choose New contact. Type the name, the person, the email and the phone. Mark what it is: client, supplier, general contractor. For a supplier, mark the cost codes it supplies (for example, siding, trim, insulation). The quote list of a project is split by supplier using these marks. Save. The contact is now available in every project.

Open Users and choose Invite. Type the email and the name, and choose the access role (see Roles and permissions). The person receives an email with a link, sets a password and signs in. The invitation expires after a few days; you can send it again. To remove access, deactivate the user. Nothing they did is deleted.

titulo: Adjust what each role can do
texto: Open Access roles and pick a role. Check or uncheck the permissions. For example, an estimator can measure but not change the catalog and not see costs. Save. The change applies the next time each person opens the system.
Open My profile to change your name, language, email or password.

Symptom Cause What to do A person cannot see Measure Takeoff Their role does not have the permission to measure. Open Access roles and turn on Measure. A person does not see prices Dollar amounts need a separate permission. Turn on the catalog or cost visibility permission for the role. The invitation email did not arrive Wrong address or spam folder. Check the address and the spam folder, then send the invitation again.
What each person can do comes from their access role. The company can adjust the default roles or create new ones (Settings › Access roles).

titulo: Permissions that matter in this release
texto: Permission What it allows Measure Open Measure Takeoff, create projects, upload plans, measure, issue proposals. Catalog Create and edit items and assemblies; see and change prices and markups. See costs See dollar amounts (cost and price) in lists and reports. Contacts Create and edit clients and suppliers. Users and roles Invite users, deactivate them and edit roles. Run bids and award Send bids, level them and award. Respond to invitations Answer invitations to bid and submit bids. Jobs Create the job from a won project (needed to close a bid). Company Edit the company profile.

Typing the address of a screen does not get around the permissions: the system checks again when it saves. Each company only ever sees its own data. Suppliers and clients are contacts, not users: they need no account.
